page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual instance built on KVM virtualization and powered by the x86_64 architecture. The server is equipped with 48 dedicated vCPUs driven by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. Accompanying the processor is 96.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory allocation profile with 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU.

The hardware configuration includes no local instance storage, requiring all persistent storage volumes and system disks to be provisioned via remote block storage. It features a baseline network bandwidth of 25 Gbps to facilitate sustained east-west data transfers and remote volume access. There are no discrete GPUs provisioned on this instance, and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned by default.

By aligning 48 dedicated processing threads with a modest memory footprint, this instance provides cost efficiency for CPU-intensive computing pipelines without incurring the expense of unneeded memory arrays. The primary architectural tradeoff is the absence of on-node ephemeral NVMe storage, meaning disk I/O performance relies entirely on attached network-based storage services.

Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.12xlarge is suited for compute-heavy workloads that scale across parallel processor cores without demanding massive memory buffers. Typical enterprise deployment targets include batch data processing, continuous integration and build nodes, parallel scientific simulation, and large-scale web or API application tiers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c8i.12xlarge is a dedicated compute-optimized instance hosted on KVM hypervisors and based on the x86_64 architecture. It provides 48 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8475B processor operating at 2.7 GHz, paired with 96.0 GB of RAM. This configuration maintains a strict 1:2 CPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU, optimizing hardware resource utilization for compute-dominated execution profiles. Networking capabilities include a baseline throughput of 25 Gbps. The server includes no local ephemeral storage, relying entirely on network-attached block devices, and contains no integrated graphics accelerators. Because compute density takes priority over memory expansion, the instance is cost-efficient for parallel tasks that require heavy processing throughput without high memory overhead. Suitable production applications include CI/CD build environments, compute-heavy microservices, batch compute queues, video encoding, and distributed scientific compute tasks.
